reason: Both documents wisely avoid the brief's unrealistic claim of doubling fresh food, sticking to the honest 50% summer increase supported by the numbers. However, Document B wins because its proposed remedy for the late 2023 report—one post-summer check-in and board tracking—is realistic for a volunteer-run group that struggled with a single report, whereas Document A's promise of quarterly updates with source-level monthly data feels like an overpromise I'd end up chasing four times a year.
